articles.title: Current concepts of management of anterior cruciate ligament revision in adults.
articles.authors: Tischer T, De Marziani L, Bait C, Bonomo M, Cavaignac E, Eriksson K, et al.
articles.study_type: Narrative review of current literature and expert consensus
articles.population: Adults undergoing anterior cruciate ligament revision surgery
articles.outcomes: Graft choice, surgical techniques, management of associated procedures, failure rates, rotational stability
articles.take_home: Anterior cruciate ligament revision is a complex procedure best suited to younger patients with high activity demands, often using autografts (the patient's own tissue) which have lower failure rates than alternatives. The review highlights that whilst surgical techniques are improving, more high-quality research is needed to establish the best approach for each individual patient, particularly regarding additional procedures to improve stability.

articles.title: Soleus subtendon elongation is reduced by individual suturing of Achilles subtendons after rupture.
articles.authors: Mikkelsen RK, Konradsen L, Hoeffner R, Krogsgaard MR, Agergaard AS, Kjaer M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with ruptured Achilles tendon
articles.sample_size: 47 patients (24 standard surgery, 23 individual suturing technique)
articles.outcomes: Soleus and gastrocnemius subtendon length measured by MRI at 1 week and 26 weeks post-surgery, expressed as side-to-side difference between injured and uninjured tendons
articles.take_home: A new surgical technique that sutures the soleus and gastrocnemius parts of a ruptured Achilles tendon separately restored the soleus tendon length much better than standard surgery one week after operation, and this advantage was maintained at six months. Both techniques resulted in some lengthening over time, but individual suturing kept this increase smaller.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic assessment of posterior cruciate ligament thickness following cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty: Relationship with functional scores.
articles.authors: Yaradilmis YU, Oguk C, Gungor O, Polat H, Ogur HU, Ciloglu O, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had cruciate-retaining total knee replacement surgery on one knee
articles.outcomes: Posterior cruciate ligament thickness measured by ultrasound in replaced and non-operated knees at mean 7.8 years follow-up; relationship between thickness difference and functional scores
articles.take_home: The ligament at the back of the knee becomes thinner after knee replacement surgery compared to the unoperated knee. Greater thinning of this ligament was linked to worse knee function scores, suggesting the ligament's condition may affect how well the knee works long term.

articles.title: Impact of social deprivation and ethnicity on patient-reported outcome measures in primary and revision hip and knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Archer JE, Sharma AD, Dunlop DJ, Gardner A, Agrawal YS
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary and revision hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures including EuroQol five-dimension questionnaire, Oxford Hip Score, and Oxford Knee Score; impact of social deprivation, ethnicity, religion, and comorbidities
articles.take_home: Patients from deprived areas, ethnic minorities, and those for whom English is not their first language reported worse outcomes before surgery and gained less improvement after surgery, suggesting healthcare inequality exists in the NHS for hip and knee replacements.

articles.title: Efficacy of Intra-Articular Corticosteroid Injection for Hip Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Kelliher A, Beilharz SA, Sutton R
articles.population: Adults with hip osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 14 studies, 3,235 participants (9 randomised trials, 5 observational studies)
articles.outcomes: Pain and physical function measured within three months and at six to twelve months post-injection
articles.take_home: Corticosteroid injections into the hip provide significant pain relief and improved function for up to three months, but this benefit does not last beyond six months. About 7% of patients experienced rapidly progressive osteoarthritis, particularly those with advanced disease at baseline, so careful patient selection is important.

articles.title: Short-Acting Spinal Anesthetics for Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Siddiqi A, Yousuf KM, Conrad D, Meneghini RM, Springer BD, Chen AF, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty or total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Length of stay, postoperative urinary retention, postoperative nausea and vomiting, readmission rates, and transient neurologic symptoms
articles.take_home: Short-acting spinal anaesthetics, particularly mepivacaine, reduced hospital stay and urinary retention compared with bupivacaine, helping patients recover faster after hip and knee replacement surgery. Lidocaine also reduced urinary retention but caused more nerve-related symptoms than other agents.

articles.title: Pseudotumor-Related Compression Neuropathies Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Panos JA, Weintraub MT, Porche KM, Sierra RJ, Abdel MP, Spinner RJ
articles.population: Patients who underwent revision total hip arthroplasty and developed pseudotumor-related compression neuropathy
articles.sample_size: 24 patients (25 hips) out of 9,042 revision procedures
articles.outcomes: Implant etiology, serum biomarkers, neurologic deficits at presentation, motor and sensory recovery following surgical decompression, postoperative dislocation rates
articles.take_home: Pseudotumor-related nerve compression after hip replacement can occur with various implant types, not just metal-on-metal bearings, and normal blood metal levels do not rule it out. Whilst surgery relieves pain effectively, recovery of nerve function is unpredictable and many patients with severe nerve damage experience persistent weakness.

articles.title: Dexamethasone is Associated with a Dose-Dependent Reduction in Venous Thromboembolic Complications following Total Knee and Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Telang SS, Wier J, Jones IA, Lim MA, Hannon CP, Lieberman JR, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national healthcare database
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing primary total knee or hip replacement between 2016 and 2023
articles.outcomes: Blood clots (venous thromboembolism) within 90 days of surgery
articles.take_home: Patients who received higher doses of dexamethasone (a steroid) during surgery had lower rates of blood clots after knee and hip replacement compared to those who received no steroid. The benefit was stronger with medium to high doses, suggesting dexamethasone may help prevent this serious complication.

articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Quantitative Indices Predict Collapse in Osteonecrosis for Lesions Occupying More Than the Medial Two-Thirds of the Weight-Bearing Portion of the Femoral Head.
articles.authors: Kawamata H, Tanaka H, Kuriyama Y, Fukuchi H, Kanabuchi R, Kurishima H, et al.
articles.population: Patients with non-traumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head, JIC Stages 1 or 2 and Types C1 or C2
articles.outcomes: Femoral head collapse (progression to JIC Stage 3A or higher) versus non-collapse (remained at Stage 2 or lower for at least 36 months)
articles.take_home: Three MRI measurements - the size of the dead bone, how deep it extends, and how deep the centre of the femoral head is affected - can help predict whether the hip will collapse. Using these measurements together was more accurate than standard X-ray classifications alone.

articles.title: Biomechanical Assessment of Pin-Site Fractures in Intra- versus Extra-Incisional Pinning Technique for Robotic Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Cadaver Study.
articles.authors: Liau ZQG, Shao-Rong Pang A, Kee Ern ET, Peng Ng MS, Meng CS, Kumarsing RA, et al.
articles.population: Matched cadaver femora and tibiae
articles.sample_size: 20 matched pairs (10 femora and 10 tibiae per group)
articles.outcomes: Torsional rigidity, fracture risk at 100 Nm and 300 Nm load, pin-site fracture involvement
articles.take_home: Placing tracker pins inside the surgical incision (intra-incisional) resulted in stronger bone and fewer fractures compared to placing them outside the incision (extra-incisional) in this cadaver study. Intra-incisional pinning may be safer for patients who start walking soon after robotic knee replacement surgery.

articles.title: Anterior cortical defects following infra-tubercle slope-reducing osteotomy show consistent remodelling without impairing union: A radiographic study with 12-month follow-up.
articles.authors: Pineda T, Patel R, Vi AK, Olivieri R, Piercecchi A, Jacquet C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing infra-tubercle slope-reducing osteotomy (high tibial osteotomy)
articles.outcomes: Anterior cortical defect remodelling measured by defect area and step-off height at 12 months; radiographic union; associations with patient factors
articles.take_home: Bone defects created during this knee surgery heal very well, with about 61 percent of the defect filling in naturally within a year and bone union occurring in nearly all patients by 6 months. Patient characteristics like age and smoking status affected healing more than the size of the initial defect.

articles.title: Cement compression device for cemented total knee arthroplasty : a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Brouwer AJ, Hesseling B, Verburg H, Goossens RHM, Mathijssen NMC
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Percentage of cemented surface at various depths in the proximal tibia; operating time
articles.take_home: A cement compression device improved how well cement bonded to the bone during knee replacement surgery, particularly in several areas around the tibia, without making the operation longer.

articles.title: Low-dose Aspirin Once Daily is Noninferior for Venous Thromboembolic Prophylaxis After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty: An Analysis of 8,073 Cases Over 10 Years.
articles.authors: Guo EW, Honey NE, Wang Z, Kaarto P, Hallstrom BR, Kheir MM
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Venous thromboembolism (blood clots) within 90 days of surgery
articles.take_home: Taking low-dose aspirin (81 mg) once daily after joint replacement surgery works just as well as taking it twice daily or stronger blood-thinning medicines at preventing dangerous blood clots. The overall risk of blood clots was low at 1.1%, with patients who had more medical conditions being at slightly higher risk.

articles.title: Equivalent Functional Recovery and Radiographic Outcomes in Human Immunodeficiency Virus-Positive and -Negative Patients Undergoing Robot-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Senyolo I, Goga N, Elebo N, Mokete L, Sikhauli N, Pietrzak JRT
articles.population: Adults undergoing robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty, comparing HIV-positive and HIV-negative patients
articles.sample_size: 214 procedures (203 patients completed three-year follow-up: 162 HIV-negative, 41 HIV-positive)
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Score, pain (Visual Analog Scale), Timed Up and Go test, range of motion, radiographic alignment, complications, patient satisfaction, and revisions
articles.take_home: Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery achieved equivalent safety and functional improvements in well-controlled HIV-positive patients compared to HIV-negative patients, with no serious complications in either group at three years. Viral suppression and nutritional status appear more important than HIV status alone when assessing surgical risk.

articles.title: Posterior Condylar Offset and Joint-Line Restoration Are Associated with Improved Patient-Reported Outcomes After Robotic-Arm-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Suhardi VJ, McCormick K, Hepinstall M, Meftah M
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-arm-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (KOOS JR) and Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) at six weeks, three months, and one year
articles.take_home: Restoring the posterior condylar offset and preserving the joint-line position during robotic-assisted knee replacement surgery was associated with better patient-reported function and less pain at three months. These findings suggest surgeons should prioritise these alignment goals to help patients recover better.

articles.title: Periprosthetic fractures after hip and knee arthroplasty in France : national trends and future projections.
articles.authors: de Geofroy B, Bulsei J, Bouche PA, Micicoi L, Fontas E, Gonzalez JF, et al.
articles.study_type: Nationwide retrospective study with future projections
articles.population: French patients undergoing reoperation for hip or knee periprosthetic fracture
articles.outcomes: Incidence rates, mortality at 3 months and 1 year, postoperative complications, projections to 2070
articles.take_home: Periprosthetic fractures (breaks around hip and knee replacements) are becoming more common in France, with the rate nearly doubling between 2015 and 2024, mainly affecting older women. These fractures carry significant risks, with 8% of patients dying within 3 months and 16% within a year, so improving prevention and care is important.

articles.title: Does Cement Viscosity Influence 10-year Outcomes in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Under Standardized Surgical Technique?
articles.authors: Lee WS, Chung H, Lee J, Chang CB
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery for aseptic loosening and radiolucent lines on X-rays
articles.take_home: Cement viscosity did not significantly affect the risk of revision surgery or loosening over 10 years when standardised surgical techniques were used. Low-viscosity cement showed a favourable trend towards lower revision rates.

articles.title: Impact of the Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement Model on Spending and Care Endpoints: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Sontag-Milobsky I, Knebel R, Edelstein AI, Ricciardi B, Rosenthal M, McGarry B, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of studies comparing outcomes before and after the Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement bundled-payment model
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip or knee arthroplasty in the United States under Medicare
articles.sample_size: 23 studies included, encompassing millions of hip and knee replacement episodes from 2011 to 2020
articles.outcomes: 90-day episode spending, complications, mortality, readmissions, length of stay, discharge destination, and procedure utilisation rates
articles.take_home: The bundled-payment model reduced costs by roughly 500 to 1,300 pounds per procedure within 90 days, mainly by reducing stays in nursing homes, without worsening safety or complication rates. However, the model appeared to favour younger and White patients whilst reducing access for Black patients and those in disadvantaged areas, raising concerns about fairness.

articles.title: Predicting Patient-Reported Outcome Measures, Satisfaction, Healthcare Utilization, Mortality, and Return to Work After Total Knee Arthroplasty Using Machine Learning: A 14,900-Patient Study.
articles.authors: Khan ST, Sharma A, Patel SV, Jevnikar BE, Rotroff D, Piuzzi NS
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with machine learning model development and validation
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative knee pain and function (KOOS subscales), patient satisfaction, hospital length of stay, discharge location, 90-day readmission, 1-year mortality, and return to work
articles.take_home: Machine learning models can predict how patients will recover after knee replacement surgery with moderate to strong accuracy, identifying which patients may have complications or slower recovery. The models used baseline information like age, weight, deprivation level, and initial knee function to make these predictions, which could help doctors plan care better before surgery.

articles.title: Patients Undergoing Manipulation Under Anesthesia Recover Mobility, but Have Worse Functional Outcomes.
articles.authors: Israelite C, Barrack R, Foran J, Cholewa J, Brook J, Redfern R, et al.
articles.study_type: Secondary data analysis of a multicenter observational cohort study
articles.population: Patients with stiff knees (less than 90 degrees active flexion at one month) after total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 270 patients (52 who had manipulation under anesthesia, 218 who did not)
articles.outcomes: Walking speed, step count, walking asymmetry, knee flexion range of motion, and knee function scores (KOOS JR)
articles.take_home: Patients who had manipulation under anesthesia recovered their walking ability within five to ten days, but reported worse knee function for up to a year compared to those who did not have the procedure. The study shows that objective measures of recovery do not always match how patients feel their knee is functioning.

articles.title: Depression as a Predictor of Postoperative Pain and Function After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Meta-Analysis of Prospective Comparative Studies.
articles.authors: Vosoughi F, Taghva Nakhjiri M, Ayati Firoozabadi A, Gholami-Chahkand MS, Sadat Fatemi N, Metanat S, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective comparative studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty with and without preoperative depression
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain, patient-reported functional outcomes (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index and Knee Society Score), and satisfaction
articles.take_home: Patients with depression start with worse pain and function before surgery and have lower absolute scores afterwards, but they improve by similar amounts to patients without depression. Depression should not stop people having knee replacement surgery, though identifying and counselling depressed patients beforehand may help manage expectations.

articles.title: Determining the Mechanical Axis of the Femur from a Standard Antero-posterior Knee Radiograph with Deep Learning.
articles.authors: Mulford KL, Grove AF, Dean MC, Saniei S, Girod-Hoffman MM, Khela M, et al.
articles.study_type: Development and validation of a deep learning algorithm
articles.population: Patients with both bilateral antero-posterior knee radiographs and long-leg radiographs taken within 90 days of each other
articles.outcomes: Mean absolute error in predicting the correction factor between anatomical and mechanical axes of the femur
articles.take_home: Researchers developed an artificial intelligence model that can predict the mechanical axis of the thigh bone from a standard knee X-ray with accuracy within 1 degree, which is better than existing methods and may help surgeons assess leg alignment more easily.

articles.title: Heterogeneity in Complication Risks and Temporal Trends Across Aseptic Indications for Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Bera SR, Brady TT, Adamczyk A, Grammatopoulos G
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using insurance claims database
articles.population: Patients undergoing first-time revision total hip arthroplasty for aseptic indications (periprosthetic fracture, dislocation, or mechanical failure)
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection, reoperation, re-revision, transfusion, readmission, and hospital stay length up to five years
articles.take_home: Revision hip surgery for different reasons carries different risks: fractures have higher infection and transfusion risks, whilst dislocations have the highest risk of needing further surgery. Infection rates have not improved over the past seven years despite improvements in other outcomes.

articles.title: Discordant Results by Study Design: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses of Mobile versus Fixed Bearing for Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Rojas-Sayol R, Martinez-Rosello A, Thabane A, Mazara A, Gil-Gonzalez S, Pelfort X, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 30 observational studies (9,454 patients), 6 randomised trials (485 patients), 3 registry studies (60,461 patients)
articles.outcomes: Revision rates, dislocation rates, Western Ontario and McMaster University Osteoarthritis Index scores, range of motion
articles.take_home: Fixed-bearing knee implants appear to have lower rates of revision and dislocation compared to mobile-bearing implants in unicompartmental knee surgery, and may improve function. However, the evidence quality is low because there are few high-quality randomised trials.

articles.title: Sustained participation deficits following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in elite male soccer players globally.
articles.authors: Khan H, Khan A, Rosenberg A, Marcaccio S
articles.population: Elite male soccer players from first or second-tier leagues globally who sustained ACL injuries between January 2007 and December 2022
articles.sample_size: 8022 unique players with 9071 ACL injuries; 4596 players included in primary analysis
articles.outcomes: Minutes played per match (MPM), number of match appearances per year, total minutes played per year, return-to-play rate
articles.take_home: While 79% of elite soccer players return to professional play after ACL reconstruction, they play significantly fewer minutes per match afterwards (10.8 minutes less on average, a 16% decrease). Players and their doctors should expect reduced match participation even after successfully returning to play.

articles.title: Anteromedializing tibial tubercle osteotomy does not restore femorotibial and patellofemoral pressures to native values in a human biomechanical model with increased femoral anteversion.
articles.authors: Morales-Avalos R, Ceniceros-Cantu C, Gutierrez-de la O J, Elizondo-Omana RE, Guzman-Lopez S, Theriot-Giron MDC, et al.
articles.study_type: Controlled biomechanical study on cadaveric specimens
articles.population: Human cadaveric knees
articles.outcomes: Intra-articular pressure measurements in patellofemoral and tibiofemoral compartments at 0, 30, 60 and 90 degrees of knee flexion
articles.take_home: Anteromedializing tibial tubercle osteotomy partially reduced abnormal joint pressures caused by increased femoral rotation, but did not fully restore pressures to normal levels. This suggests that surgery addressing only the lower leg may not be enough when there is significant rotational deformity of the thigh bone, and surgeons should consider treating the upper leg as well.

articles.title: Posterior tibial slope is linearly related to anteroposterior shift of the tibiofemoral contact mechanics: A biomechanical study.
articles.authors: Peez C, Palma Kries LK, Grose-Allermann A, Leibrandt L, Deichsel A, Briese T, et al.
articles.population: Fresh-frozen cadaveric knees
articles.outcomes: Anteroposterior and mediolateral centre of force migration, contact area, mean pressure and peak pressure at different tibial slope angles and knee flexion positions, with and without ACL
articles.take_home: Reducing the slope of the tibia at the knee moves the contact point forwards, which reduces pressure on the back of the knee joint. This effect is stronger when the ACL is damaged, suggesting that slope-reducing surgery might help protect the back of the knee in patients with recurrent ACL instability.

articles.title: Knee joint line obliquity alters lateral meniscal root tension, tibiofemoral subluxation and compartment-specific contact pressures.
articles.authors: Nejima S, Bonacic-Bartolin P, Ball S, Williams A, van Arkel R, Amis A
articles.study_type: Laboratory biomechanical study on cadaver knees
articles.population: Eight human knee specimens
articles.outcomes: Meniscal root tension, tibiofemoral subluxation and compartment contact pressures under different joint line angles
articles.take_home: The angle of the knee joint line affects how much tension is placed on the lateral meniscus and changes contact pressure in the knee. Surgeons should consider the joint line angle when planning knee alignment procedures.

articles.title: Forecasting knee arthroplasty surgery with deep learning : an integrated approach using routine clinical data and radiographs.
articles.authors: Musbahi O, Hall TAG, Alibert A, Jones GG, Cobb J, van Arkel RJ
articles.study_type: Development and validation of a deep learning prediction model
articles.population: Patients with or at risk of knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 3,026 patients in primary cohort (MOST dataset); external validation with OAI dataset
articles.outcomes: Prediction of need for knee arthroplasty and time to surgery using combined clinical data and knee radiographs
articles.take_home: A computer model combining patient information and knee X-rays can accurately predict whether someone will need knee replacement surgery and when it might be needed. The model performed well when tested on different patient groups, suggesting it could help NHS services plan resources and give patients timely access to surgery.

articles.title: Undernourished and Underweight: Independent Predictors of Worse Outcomes Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Choubey A, Abunnur N, Hussain J, Babul C, Farid YR, Gonzalez MH
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national surgical database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty with BMI less than 25
articles.outcomes: 30-day postoperative complications including bleeding, cardiac arrest, readmission, death, and urinary tract infection
articles.take_home: Underweight patients and those with low protein levels (hypoalbuminemia) had significantly higher rates of serious complications after hip replacement surgery, including bleeding, heart problems, and death. Patients with both low weight and low protein levels faced the highest risks, suggesting that nutritional assessment before surgery may help identify and support vulnerable patients.

articles.title: Preoperative Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement Scores Predict Timing and Achievement of Substantial Clinical Benefit Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Carender CN, Wang Z, Janney C, Hallstrom BR, Dailey EA, Kheir MM
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Timing and rate of substantial clinical benefit (improvement of at least 22 points in Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement) achievement within one year after surgery
articles.take_home: Most patients (83%) achieved substantial clinical benefit from hip replacement within one year, with the median time to this improvement being 80 days. Patients with worse hip function before surgery improved faster, whilst those with less severe symptoms before surgery were more likely to not reach substantial clinical benefit by one year.

articles.title: The Effect of Dual Mobility Articulations on Re-Revision After Revision for Dislocation.
articles.authors: Zamzam M, Hodson N, Zhu Q, Zheng H, Hallstrom B, Charters M
articles.population: Patients who underwent revision hip replacement surgery for dislocation after initial hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Re-revision rates at 1, 2, and 5 years after revision surgery; comparison of dual mobility versus fixed-bearing acetabular constructs
articles.take_home: Dual mobility hip implants were associated with lower rates of repeat revision surgery in the first two years after revision for instability, with about 6-7% fewer patients needing further surgery. However, the benefit may decrease over longer follow-up periods.

articles.title: Trochanteric Osteotomy in Two-Stage Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty for Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Entezari B, Hakim R, Cao K, Alrefai S, Axelrod D, Safir OA, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing two-stage revision surgery for hip joint infection
articles.outcomes: Operative time, blood loss, intraoperative femoral fractures, postoperative complications, infection control, ambulatory status
articles.take_home: Using trochanteric osteotomy (a surgical technique that involves cutting the hip bone) took longer during the first operation but prevented intraoperative fractures of the thighbone, which occurred in patients who did not have this technique. Both approaches achieved similar infection control and complication rates overall.

articles.title: Cefazolin Prophylaxis in Patients Over 120 Kilograms: Comparison of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Following Total Hip Arthroplasty With Two Versus Three Grams Dosing.
articles.authors: Hurka KL, Rumalla KC, Memon R, Sohn MO, Desai RM, Edelstein AI
articles.population: Adults weighing over 120 kilograms undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 90-day periprosthetic joint infection rates with two versus three grams cefazolin prophylaxis
articles.take_home: There was no significant difference in infection rates between patients given two grams and three grams of cefazolin after hip replacement surgery, although three grams showed a moderate probability of reducing infection risk in further analysis. The study does not provide clear evidence to change current dosing recommendations.

articles.title: Trauma-Related Arthroplasty Is Associated With Earlier and Microbiologically Distinct Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A 20-Year Single-Center Study.
articles.authors: Moynan D, O'Connor C, Woo J, Kenny C, Brady D, O'hEireamhoin S, et al.
articles.population: Adults with periprosthetic joint infection following arthroplasty, comparing trauma-related cases (such as hip fracture) with elective procedures
articles.outcomes: Treatment success at 12 months (defined as stopping antibiotics, functional joint restoration, and no recurrent infection), time from arthroplasty to infection, microbiology of infections, and six-month mortality
articles.take_home: Infections after trauma-related joint replacement happen earlier (12 weeks versus 56 weeks) and involve different types of bacteria than infections after routine replacement, with higher early death rates. However, treatment success rates at 12 months were similar between the two groups.

articles.title: Patient-specific talar resurfacing improves pain and function at 24 months in osteochondral lesions of the talus.
articles.authors: Mosca M, Di Ponte M, Cassanelli E, Bonaiuti M, Gardini G, Van Dijk N, et al.
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic osteochondral lesions of the talus
articles.outcomes: Pain scores, Foot and Ankle Outcome Score (FAOS), quality of life, return to sport and work, complications and reoperations
articles.take_home: A custom-made implant to resurface damaged cartilage on the ankle bone significantly reduced pain and improved function and quality of life at two years, with most patients able to return to sport and work. However, the study was small and longer-term studies are needed to confirm these benefits last.

articles.title: Sport participation after isolated distal femoral osteotomy in young patients: High return-to-sport rates and predictive role of preoperative activity level.
articles.authors: Lucidi GA, Adravanti FM, Rossi C, Bonaiuti M, Di Paolo S, Grassi A, et al.
articles.population: Young, physically active patients under 45 years old with lateral knee pain and valgus malalignment treated with distal femoral osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Return to sport rate, sports participation level, return to work rate, and complications at mean 7.2 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Around 79% of young active patients returned to sport after distal femoral osteotomy, with most maintaining their previous sport level, and all patients returned to work. Patients who were more active before symptoms were more likely to return to sport.

articles.title: Previous bariatric surgery was not associated with an increased risk of reintervention within 2 years after knee arthroplasty: A nationwide register-based study from Denmark.
articles.authors: Aljuboori SM, Petersen J, Christensen R, Jimenez-Solem E, Karhus LL, Overgaard S
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis undergoing knee arthroplasty, with and without previous bariatric surgery
articles.sample_size: 1427 patients with previous bariatric surgery matched with 6194 controls
articles.outcomes: Reintervention rates at 90 days and 2 years, infection-related revision, and mortality within 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients who had bariatric surgery before knee replacement had no higher risk of needing further surgery or dying within 2 years compared to patients who had not had bariatric surgery, regardless of their weight at the time of knee replacement.

articles.title: Mechanisms and situational patterns of anterior cruciate ligament injuries in professional women's football (soccer): A systematic video analysis across 25 leagues (2022-2024).
articles.authors: Hampstead W, Lovell R, Whalan M, Chia L, Bonney J, Wakefield B, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic video analysis of professional women's football matches
articles.population: Professional women's football players sustaining anterior cruciate ligament injuries across international and national leagues
articles.sample_size: 247 ACL injuries identified; 127 with video footage analysed
articles.outcomes: Biomechanical characteristics and contextual patterns of ACL injuries including injury timing, match phase, mechanism of injury, player actions, and knee positioning during injury
articles.take_home: Most ACL injuries in professional women's football happen during the first half while defending, usually without direct contact to the knee. The injuries typically occurred during pressing or tackling actions where players had their knees slightly bent with outward knee collapse.

articles.title: The New Munich Elbow Soft Tissue (MEST) classification is a reliable MRI-based injury severity grading system for acute simple elbow dislocations.
articles.authors: Wackerle AM, Vieider RP, Kadantsev P, Marka A, Leonhardt Y, Kluge M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with acute simple elbow dislocation presenting to a trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Inter- and intrarater reliability of the MEST classification using MRI assessment; Fleiss' kappa 0.690 for MEST grade and 0.639 for MEST subclassification
articles.take_home: The new MEST classification system reliably grades soft tissue damage after simple elbow dislocations using MRI scans, with moderate to substantial agreement between different assessors. This classification could help doctors consistently assess injury severity and guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Initial stability of surface vs. full cemented tibial components under cyclic loading.
articles.authors: Khan M, Moldestad IO, Ellison P, Gjertsen JE, Hol PJ, Furnes ON
articles.population: Composite tibia models with NexGen Stemmed Option tibial baseplates
articles.outcomes: Implant migration, micromotion, and bonding strength under cyclic loading; correlation between cement thickness and implant movement
articles.take_home: Fully cementing the tibial component resulted in less forward movement and micromotion, and stronger bonding than surface cementation alone. Thicker cement at the front of the implant was associated with less movement.

articles.title: Incidence, cost, and risk factors for early sepsis following revision total knee arthroplasty for periprosthetic joint infection.
articles.authors: Elmenawi KA, Khan ST, Patel SV, Pasqualini I, Gudapati LS, Higuera CA, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing first-time revision total knee replacement for infection
articles.outcomes: Incidence of sepsis within 90 days of surgery; risk factors for sepsis; healthcare costs
articles.take_home: About 14 out of every 100 patients developed serious infection within 90 days after revision knee replacement for a previous infection. Patients who developed sepsis had higher costs and were more likely to be male, have kidney problems, smoke, be obese, or have low protein levels.

articles.title: Validation of a standardized question and a numerical rating scale for assessment of patient satisfaction after knee arthroplasty at one and two years.
articles.authors: Clement ND, Karimaghaei D, Afzal I, Haddad FS, Kader DF
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 7,644 knee replacements in 6,690 patients; 5,893 with one-year follow-up and 4,879 with two-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction using a 0 to 100 numerical rating scale at one and two years after surgery, with validation against Oxford Knee Scores and EQ-5D-3L scores
articles.take_home: A simple 0 to 100 satisfaction question is a reliable and valid way to measure how happy patients are after knee replacement surgery. The study suggests checking satisfaction at one year is best, as satisfaction does not improve further by two years.
